Department of Justice
Drug Enforcement Administration
On March 17, 2026, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA or Government) issued an Order to Show Cause (OSC) to Youmna Abdulhadi, M.D., of El Centro, California (Registrant). Request for Final Agency Action (RFAA), Exhibit (RFAAX) 2, at 1, 3. The OSC proposed the revocation of Registrant's Certificate of Registration No. FA2682967, alleging that Registrant is “currently without authority to prescribe, administer, dispense, or otherwise handle controlled substances in the State of California, the state in which [she is] registered with DEA.”
Id.
at 2. (citing
21 U.S.C. 824(a)(3)
).
[
1
]
The OSC notified Registrant of her right to file a written request for hearing, and that if she failed to file such a request, she would be deemed to have waived her right to a hearing and be in default.
Id.
at 2 (citing
21 CFR 1301.43
). Here, Registrant did not request a hearing, and the Agency finds her to be in default. RFAA, at 3.
[
2
]
“A default,
(
printed page 66364)
unless excused, shall be deemed to constitute a waiver of the registrant's/applicant's right to a hearing and an admission of the factual allegations of the [OSC].”
21 CFR 1301.43(e)
.
Further, “[i]n the event that a registrant . . . is deemed to be in default . . . DEA may then file a request for final agency action with the Administrator, along with a record to support its request. In such circumstances, the Administrator may enter a default final order pursuant to [21 CFR] 1316.67.”
Id.
at 1301.43(f)(1). Here, the Government has requested final agency action based on Registrant's default pursuant to
21 CFR 1301.43(c)
,
(f)
, and
1301.46
. RFAA, at 4;
see
21 CFR 1316.67
.
Findings of Fact
The Agency finds that, in light of Registrant's default, the factual allegations in the OSC are deemed admitted.
21 CFR 1301.43(e)
. According to the OSC, effective December 4, 2024, the Medical Board of California revoked Registrant's California medical license. RFAAX 2, at 2. According to California online records, of which the Agency takes official notice,
[
3
]
Registrant's California medical license has a primary status of “License Revoked.” California DCA License Search,
https://search.dca.ca.gov
(last visited date of signature of this Order). Accordingly, the Agency finds that Registrant is not licensed to practice medicine in California, the state in which she is registered with DEA.
[
4
]
Discussion
Pursuant to
21 U.S.C. 824(a)(3)
, the Attorney General is authorized to suspend or revoke a registration issued under
21 U.S.C. 823
“upon a finding that the registrant . . . has had his State license or registration suspended . . . [or] revoked . . . by competent State authority and is no longer authorized by State law to engage in the . . . dispensing of controlled substances.”
With respect to a practitioner, DEA has also long held that the possession of authority to dispense controlled substances under the laws of the state in which a practitioner engages in professional practice is a fundamental condition for obtaining and maintaining a practitioner's registration.
Gonzales
v.
Oregon,
546 U.S. 243, 270 (2006) (“The Attorney General can register a physician to dispense controlled substances `if the applicant is authorized to dispense . . . controlled substances under the laws of the State in which he practices.' . . . The very definition of a `practitioner' eligible to prescribe includes physicians `licensed, registered, or otherwise permitted, by the United States or the jurisdiction in which he practices' to dispense controlled substances. 802(21).”). The Agency has applied these principles consistently.
See, e.g., James L. Hooper, M.D.,
76 FR 71371
,
71372
(2011),
pet. for rev. denied,
481 F. App'x 826 (4th Cir. 2012);
Frederick Marsh Blanton, M.D.,
43 FR 27616
,
27617
(1978).
[
5
]
According to California statute, “dispense” means “to deliver a controlled substance to an ultimate user or research subject by or pursuant to the lawful order of a practitioner, including the prescribing, furnishing, packaging, labeling, or compounding necessary to prepare the substance for that delivery.” Cal. Health & Safety Code § 11010 (West 2026). Further, a “practitioner” means a person “licensed, registered, or otherwise permitted, to distribute, dispense, conduct research with respect to, or administer, a controlled substance in the course of professional practice or research in [the] state.”
Id.
§  11026(c).
Here, the undisputed evidence in the record is that Registrant currently lacks authority to practice medicine in California. As discussed above, an individual must be a licensed practitioner to dispense a controlled substance in California. Thus, because Registrant currently lacks authority to practice medicine in California and, therefore, is not authorized to handle controlled substances in California, Registrant is not eligible to maintain a DEA registration. Accordingly, the Agency will order that Registrant's DEA registration be revoked.
Order
Pursuant to
28 CFR 0.100(b)
and the authority vested in me by
21 U.S.C. 824(a)
, I hereby revoke DEA Certificate of Registration No. FA2682967 issued to Youmna Abdulhadi, M.D. Further, pursuant to
28 CFR 0.100(b)
and the authority vested in me by
21 U.S.C. 823(g)(1)
, I hereby deny any pending applications of Youmna Abdulhadi, M.D., to renew or modify this registration, as well as any other pending application of Youmna Abdulhadi, M.D., for additional registration in California. This Order is effective November 19, 2026.
Signing Authority
This document of the Drug Enforcement Administration was signed on October 14, 2026, by DEA Administrator Terrance C. Cole. That document with the original signature and date is maintained by DEA. For administrative purposes only, and in compliance with requirements of the Office of the Federal Register, the undersigned DEA Federal Register Liaison Officer has been authorized to sign and submit the document in electronic format for publication, as an official document of DEA. This administrative process in no way alters
(
printed page 66365)
the legal effect of this document upon publication in the
Federal Register
.
Heather Achbach,
Federal Register Liaison Officer, Drug Enforcement Administration.
Footnotes
1.
    
                         According to Agency records, Registrant's registration expired on June 30, 2026. The fact that a registrant allows her registration to expire during the pendency of an OSC does not impact the Agency's jurisdiction or prerogative under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA) to adjudicate the OSC to finality.
Jeffrey D. Olsen, M.D.,
84 FR 68474
,
68476-68479
(2019).
Back to Citation
2.
    
                         Based on the Government's submissions in its RFAA dated June 23, 2026, the Agency finds that service of the OSC on Registrant was adequate. The included declaration from a DEA Diversion Investigator (DI) indicates that on or about March 30, 2026, the DI traveled with a Special Agent (SA) to Registrant's last known residential address to attempt in-person service but was unsuccessful. RFAAX 3, at 2. On the same date, the DI emailed Registrant a copy of the OSC at her registered email address.
Id.
at 3;
see also id.,
Attachment C. On or about March 31, 2026, the DI traveled with another SA and a Task Force Officer (TFO) to Registrant's 
                        
                        registered address to attempt in-person service but was again unsuccessful.
Id.
at 3. On the same date, the DI also mailed a copy of the OSC to Registrant's registered address.
Id.
On or about April 1, 2026, the DI mailed another copy of the OSC to a newly discovered address associated with Registrant.
Id.
Finally, on the same date, the DI emailed a copy of the OSC to two newly discovered email addresses associated with Registrant.
Id.; see also id.,
Attachments D-E. Here, the Agency finds that Registrant was successfully served the OSC by email and that the DI's efforts to serve Registrant by other means were “ `reasonably calculated, under all the circumstances, to apprise [Registrant] of the pendency of the action.' ”
Jones
v.
Flowers,
547 U.S. 220, 226 (2006) (quoting
Mullane
v.
Central Hanover Bank & Trust Co.,
339 U.S. 306, 314 (1950)). Therefore, due process notice requirements have been satisfied.
See Mohammed S. Aljanaby, M.D.,
82 FR 34552
,
34552
(2017) (finding that service by email satisfies due process where the email is not returned as undeliverable and other methods have been unsuccessful);
Emilio Luna, M.D.,
77 FR 4829
,
4830
(2012) (same).
Back to Citation
3.
    
                         Under the Administrative Procedure Act, an agency “may take official notice of facts at any stage in a proceeding—even in the final decision.” United States Department of Justice, Attorney General's Manual on the Administrative Procedure Act 80 (1947) (Wm. W. Gaunt & Sons, Inc., Reprint 1979).
Back to Citation
4.
    
                         Pursuant to
5 U.S.C. 556(e)
, “[w]hen an agency decision rests on official notice of a material fact not appearing in the evidence in the record, a party is entitled, on timely request, to an opportunity to show the contrary.” The material fact here is that Registrant, as of the date of this Order, is not licensed to practice medicine in California. Accordingly, Registrant may dispute the Agency's finding by filing a properly supported motion for reconsideration of findings of fact within fifteen calendar days of the date of this Order. Any such motion and response shall be filed and served by email to the other party and to the Office of the Administrator, Drug Enforcement Administration, at
dea.addo.attorneys@dea.gov
.
Back to Citation
5.
    
                         This rule derives from the text of two provisions of the CSA. First, Congress defined the term “practitioner” to mean “a physician . . . or other person licensed, registered, or otherwise permitted, by . . . the jurisdiction in which he practices . . . , to distribute, dispense, . . . [or] administer . . . a controlled substance in the course of professional practice.”
21 U.S.C. 802(21)
. Second, in setting the requirements for obtaining a practitioner's registration, Congress directed that “[t]he Attorney General shall register practitioners . . . if the applicant is authorized to dispense . . . controlled substances under the laws of the State in which he practices.”
21 U.S.C. 823(g)(1)
. Because Congress has clearly mandated that a practitioner possess state authority in order to be deemed a practitioner under the CSA, DEA has held repeatedly that revocation of a practitioner's registration is the appropriate sanction whenever he is no longer authorized to dispense controlled substances under the laws of the state in which he practices.
See, e.g., James L. Hooper, M.D.,
76 FR at 71371-72;
Sheran Arden Yeates, M.D.,
71 FR 39130
,
39131
(2006);
Dominick A. Ricci, M.D.,
58 FR 51104
,
51105
(1993);
Bobby Watts, M.D.,
53 FR 11919
,
11920
(1988);
Frederick Marsh Blanton, M.D.,
43 FR at 27617.
Back to Citation

Title:

Summary of Collection:
The Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) has been delegated the authority to exercise the functions of the Secretary as provided in the Federal Meat Inspection Act (FMIA) (
21 U.S.C. 601
et seq.
), the Poultry Products Inspection Act (PPIA) (
21 U.S.C. 451
et seq.
), and the Egg Products Inspection Act (EPIA) (
21 U.S.C. 1031
et seq.
). These statutes mandate that FSIS protect the public by ensuring that meat, poultry, and egg products are safe, wholesome, and properly labeled. The Federal Meat Inspection Act (
21 U.S.C. 642
), the Poultry Products Inspection Act (
21 U.S.C. 460
(b)) require certain parties to keep records that clearly show every business transaction involving animal carcasses and parts.
FSIS requires FSIS accredited non-Federal analytical laboratories to maintain certain information collection records. FSIS collects this information using FSIS forms 10,000-7, 10,120-1a, 10,120-1b, 10,120-1c, and 10,120-1d.
Need and Use of the Information:
FSIS collects information to ensure that non-federal laboratories operate in accordance with FSIS regulations. In addition, FSIS also collects information to ensure that meat and poultry establishments exempted from Agency inspection do not commingle inspected and non-inspected meat and poultry products, and to ensure that retail operations determined to have violated the requirements associated with retail exemptions keep sales purchase and sales records to ensure future compliance. If the information was not collected or collected less frequently it would reduce the effectiveness of FSIS inspection programs.

AGENCY:
Department of Defense (DoD).
ACTION:
Notice of Federal Advisory Committee meeting.
SUMMARY:
The DoD (referred to herein as “the Department”, “Department of War” or “DoW”) is publishing this notice to announce the following federal advisory committee meeting of the Defense Policy Board (DPB) will take place.
DATES:
Closed to the public; Tuesday, October 20, 2026, from 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Wednesday, October 21, 2026, from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. The closed meetings will be held in the Rodman Conference Room, 3D852, at The Pentagon, 2000 Defense Pentagon, Washington, DC 20301-2000.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
James E. Benkowski, DPB Designated Federal Officer (DFO), 703-697-4758 (Voice),
james.e.benkowski2.civ@mail.mil
(Email). Mailing address is 2000 Defense Pentagon, Attn: 5E420, Washington, DC 20301-2000.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
This meeting is being held under the provisions of 5 United States Code (U.S.C.) chapter 10 of (commonly known as the “Federal Advisory Committee Act” or “FACA”);
5 U.S.C. 552b
(commonly known as the “Government in the Sunshine Act”); and 41 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) parts 102-3.140 and 102-3.150. Due to circumstances beyond the control of the (DFO, the DPB was unable to provide public notification required by
41 CFR part 102-3.150(a)
concerning its October 20-21, 2026, meeting. Accordingly, the Advisory Committee Management Officer for the Department of War (DoW), pursuant to
41 CFR part 102-3.150(b)
, waives the seven-calendar day notification requirement.
Purpose of the Meeting:
To obtain, review, and evaluate classified information related to the DPB's mission to assess the defense implications of various trade and economic policy issues as they relate to the DoW, including on: (a) How the DoW can best support and integrate with the Administration's trade and international economic strategy; (b) supercharging our Defense Industrial Base; (c) increasing burden-sharing with allies and partners; and (d) the potential effects and strategic implications of “China Shock 2.0.”
Agenda:
On October 20 and 21, 2026, the DPB will receive classified briefings to assess the defense implications of various trade and economic policy issues as they relate to DoW strategic planning and other national security policy issues.
Dr. James Benkowski, DPB DFO, will provide opening remarks; HON Elbridge Colby, Under Secretary of War for Policy (USW(P)), and AMB Robert Lighthizer, DPB Chair, will welcome the DPB and provide an overview of the meeting's purpose and its key objectives focused on the implications of various trade and economic policy issues. Subject matter experts from the USW (P) and the Office of the General Counsel will provide training on security and ethics, respectively, in an administrative session.
Mr. James Ruocco, Performing the Duties of Assistant Secretary of War for Acquisition, will explain the DoW's approach to acquisition reform and supercharging the Defense Industrial Base in alignment with President Trump and Secretary Hegseth's guidance; and identify key issues for the DPB's consideration and action.
Ambassador Jamieson Greer, United States Trade Representative, and HON Elbridge Colby, USW(P), will discuss ways that DoW strategic planning can best support and integrate with the Administration's trade and international economic strategy.
Mr. Tom Sisk, Defense Intelligence Officer for China, will provide an intelligence update regarding Chinese perceptions on U.S. trade and economic policy as well as how potential responses to “China Shock 2.0” may influence the People's Republic of China calculus and behavior.
AMB Robert Lighthizer will lead the DPB in drawing on its own expertise and experience to discuss key challenges and opportunities regarding the Administration's trade and economic strategy, and to deliberate in order to develop advice and recommendations for the Secretary of
(
printed page 66319)
War and the Deputy Secretary of War through the USW(P).
Mr. David Copley, Senior Director, National Security Council, will lead a discussion with DPB members to better understand the administration's approach to securing supply chains and critical minerals.
AMB Robert Lighthizer will again lead the DPB in drawing on its own expertise and experience to discuss key challenges and opportunities regarding the Administration's trade and economic strategy, and to deliberate in order to develop advice and recommendations for the Secretary of War and the Deputy Secretary of War through the USW(P).
The DPB will then provide advice and recommendations to HON Elbridge Colby, USW(P).
Meeting Accessibility:
In accordance with
5 U.S.C. 1009(d)
and
41 CFR part 102-3.155
, the DoW has determined that this meeting shall be closed to the public. The USW(P), in consultation with the DoW FACA Attorney, has determined in writing that this meeting is closed to the public because the discussions fall under the purview of
5 U.S.C. 552b(c)(1)
and are so inextricably intertwined with unclassified material that they cannot reasonably be segregated into separate discussions without disclosing classified material.
Written Statements:
In accordance with
5 U.S.C. 1009(a)(3)
and
41 CFR parts 102-3.140(c)
and 102-3.150(6) the public or interested organizations may submit written statements to the membership of the DPB at any time regarding its mission or in response to the stated agenda of a planned meeting. Written statements should be submitted to the DPB's DFO, who's information is listed above in this notice in the
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT
section or can be obtained from the General Services Administration (GSA) FACA Database—
http://www.facadatabase.gov/​
.
Written statements that do not pertain to a scheduled meeting of the DPB may be submitted at any time. However, if individual comments pertain to a specific topic being discussed at a planned meeting, then these statements must be submitted no later than one business day prior to the meeting in question in order for the DPB to consider the statement prior to or during the meeting. The DFO will review all submitted written statements and provide copies to all DPB members. Please note that all submitted comments and statements will be treated as public documents and will be made available for public inspection.
Dated: October 15, 2026.
Stephanie J. Bost,
Alternate OSD Federal Register Liaison Officer, Department of Defense.

AGENCY:
Federal Railroad Administration (FRA), Federal Transit Administration (FTA), U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT).
ACTION:
Notice, request for comments.
SUMMARY:
This notice announces that FRA and FTA (Agencies) have received and reviewed an application package from the State of Utah (State), Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT), requesting participation in the Surface Transportation Project Delivery Program (Program). Under the Program, the Agencies may assign, and a State may assume, responsibilities under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), and all or part of the Agencies' responsibilities for environmental review, consultation, or other actions required under any Federal environmental laws except certain statutory exclusions with respect to one or more railroad projects and one or more public transportation projects within the State. The Agencies have determined the application package to be complete and developed a draft Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the State outlining how UDOT will implement the Program with the Agencies' oversight. The public is invited to comment on UDOT's request, including its application package and the proposed MOU, which includes the proposed assignments and assumptions of environmental review, consultation, and other activities.
DATES:
Comments must be received on or before November 19, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
Comments related to Docket No. FRA-2026-2740 may be submitted by going to
https://www.regulations.gov
and following the online instructions for submitting comments.
Instructions:
All submissions must refer to the Federal Railroad Administration, the Federal Transit Administration, and the docket number in this notice (FRA-2026-2740). Note that all submissions received, including any personal information provided, will be posted without change and will be

https://www.regulations.gov
.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
Section 327 of Title 23, United States Code
(
23 U.S.C. 327
) establishes the Surface Transportation Project Delivery Program, also referred to as the NEPA Assignment Program (Program). It allows the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Transportation (Secretary) to assign, and a State to assume, responsibility for all or part of the Secretary's responsibilities for environmental review, consultation, or other actions required under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) (
42 U.S.C. 4321-4370h
) and any Federal environmental law with respect to one or more highway projects within the State, as well as one or more railroad, public transportation, and/or multimodal projects. FRA is authorized to act on behalf of the Secretary with respect to these matters for railroad projects and FTA is authorized to act on behalf of the Secretary with respect to these matters for public transportation projects.
The State of Utah initially participated in the Federal Highway Administration's (FHWA's) Program. In accordance with
23 U.S.C. 327
, the NEPA Assignment Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was executed between the State, acting through UDOT, and FHWA and became effective on January 17, 2017. After the initial MOU term, the agreement was renewed on May 26, 2022. Since being accepted into the FHWA NEPA Assignment Program, the State has successfully completed four audits, seven self-assessments, and one monitoring event. FHWA has consistently publicly stated that the State continues to meet all requirements of the NEPA Assignment Program. The State will have participated in the Program for 10 years on December 17, 2027.
Pursuant to
23 CFR 773.107(b)(1)
and
(2)
, UDOT provided public notice of its draft joint application requesting FRA and FTA NEPA assignment responsibilities on July 29, 2026. It was available for a 30-day comment period, with comments due by the close of business on August 28, 2026. The notice was published in a statewide newspaper and is available at:
https://connect.udot.utah.gov/​events/​notice-of-availability-of-the-utah-department-of-transportations-application-to-assume-the-federal-railroad-administrations-and-federal-transit-administrations-nepa-responsi/​
.
UDOT also sent notice of the joint application by email and letter with request for comment to all transit agencies in Utah, metropolitan planning organizations, regional planning organizations, associations of governments, regulatory agencies, and Native American Tribes. UDOT notified State agencies through the State of Utah's Resource Development Coordination Council, which is responsible for notifying all State agencies and compiling any comments received related to actions that may affect the physical resources of the State. On September 3, 2026, UDOT formally submitted its joint application package to the Agencies. The submission includes a verification of Statewide notice and solicitation of public comment, Utah's determination that the State of Utah's Public Records Act is comparable to the Federal Freedom of Information Act, the draft MOU, and the UDOT Commissioner's signature approving the application.
Under the proposed MOU, the Agencies would assign to the State the responsibility for making decisions on railroad and public transportation projects as described in UDOT's application and in Part 2 of the draft MOU. As provided in subpart 2.3, UDOT is requesting to assume the Agencies' responsibilities under NEPA for the following covered classes of railroad and public transportation projects upon execution of the Program MOU with the Agencies: all railroad projects in Utah whose source of Federal funding comes from FRA or require FRA approvals; all public transportation projects in Utah whose source of Federal funding comes from FTA or requires FTA approvals; and all projects funded by other Federal agencies, or projects without any Federal funding, that also require FRA or FTA approvals. As provided in subparts 2.1.1 and 2.1.2, UDOT is requesting to assume the Agencies' responsibilities under NEPA for these covered railroad and public transportation projects where UDOT is the Direct Recipient and responsible for the design (for FTA) or final design (for FRA) and construction of the project, or where UDOT is designated in a project-specific agreement as the project sponsor or co-sponsor. For these projects, UDOT requests to assume only the Agencies' NEPA responsibilities; the request does not include assuming the NEPA responsibilities of other Federal agencies. UDOT may assume the Agencies' responsibilities under NEPA for locally administered railroad or public transportation projects by mutual agreement between the State and FRA or FTA, as applicable, pursuant to the requirements of
23 U.S.C. 327(l)
. In addition, UDOT would establish appropriate relationships with other Operating Administration(s) involved in a multimodal project, including cooperating agency, participating agency, and lead or co-lead agency relationships under NEPA. Lastly, UDOT may rely on other Federal agencies' NEPA analyses consistent with NEPA, USDOT, FRA and FTA regulations, policies, and guidance, as applicable. UDOT's assumption of these NEPA Assignment responsibilities will provide for the highest degree of program-wide consistency and efficiency in document review and agency coordination. It will also provide the greatest opportunity for streamlining benefits.
Excluded from assignment are the following:
(1) Railroad or public transportation projects that cross State boundaries or that cross or are adjacent to international boundaries. For purposes of the State's application and the proposed MOU, a project is considered “adjacent to international boundaries” if it requires the issuance of a new, or modification of an existing, Presidential Permit.
(2) As provided at
23 U.S.C. 327(a)(2)(D)
, any railroad or public transportation project that is not assumed by the State as identified in the State's application and under subparts 2.3 through 2.6 of the proposed MOU, remains the responsibility of FRA or FTA.
Under the proposed MOU, UDOT would also assume the responsibility to conduct the following environmental review, reevaluation, consultation, or other action pertaining to the review or approval of railroad and public transportation projects specified under MOU subpart 2.3 and required under the following Federal environmental laws and executive orders related to

The proposed MOU would allow UDOT to act in the place of FRA and FTA in carrying out the environmental review-related functions described above, except with respect to Government-to-Government consultations with federally recognized Indian Tribes. UDOT would continue to handle routine consultations with the Tribes and understands that a Tribe has the right to direct consultation with FRA or FTA upon request. UDOT may assist FRA or FTA with Government-to-Government consultations, with consent of a Tribe, but FRA and FTA remain responsible for the consultation.
In addition, UDOT would not assume FRA's or FTA's responsibilities for conformity determinations required under Section 176 of the CAA (
42 U.S.C. 7506
), or any responsibility under
23 U.S.C. 134
or
135
, or under
49 U.S.C. 5303
or
5304
.
FRA and FTA will consider the comments submitted on UDOT's joint application and the proposed MOU. A copy of the joint application package and proposed MOU may be viewed on the docket (FRA-2026-2740) at
https://www.regulations.gov
.
A copy also may be viewed on UDOT's website at:
https://connect.udot.utah.gov/​about-us/​program-development-group/​environmental-division/​
.
Any final MOU approved by FRA and FTA may include changes based on comments and consultations relating to the proposed MOU and will be made publicly available.

Department of State
[Public Notice:13150]
Pursuant to section 404 of the CSPA (
22 U.S.C.2370c-1
) and presidential delegation of authority dated August 4, 2025, I hereby: Determine that it is in the national interest of the United States to waive in part the application of the prohibition in section 404(a) of the CSPA with respect to the Central African Republic to allow for the provision of international military education and training (IMET) assistance and excess defense articles (EDA) and the issuance of direct commercial sales (DCS) licenses to the extent that the CSPA would restrict such assistance; to waive in part the application of the prohibition in section 404(a) of the CSPA with respect to the DRC to allow for the provision of IMET and peacekeeping operations (PKO) assistance, and the issuance of DCS licenses to the extent that the CSPA would restrict such assistance; to waive the application of the prohibition in section 404(a) of the CSPA with respect to Ethiopia; to waive the application of the prohibition in section 404(a) of the CSPA with respect to Nigeria; to waive in part the application of the prohibition in section 404(a) of the CSPA with respect to Somalia to allow for the provision of PKO assistance and support provided pursuant to
10 U.S.C. 331
and
10 U.S.C. 333
to the extent that the CSPA would restrict such assistance; to waive in part the application of the prohibition in section 404(a) of the CSPA with respect to Venezuela to allow for the provision of IMET assistance to the extent that the CSPA would restrict such assistance; to waive the application of the prohibition in section 404(a) of the CSPA with respect to Yemen; and to waive the application of the prohibition in section 404(a) of the CSPA to allow for the issuance of DCS licenses related to other U.S. government assistance for the above countries and, with respect to the Russian Federation, solely for the issuance of DCS licenses in connection with the International Space Station.
I certify that the governments of the above countries are taking effective and continuing steps to address the problem of child soldiers.
Accordingly, I hereby waive such applications of section 404(a) of the CSPA.
This determination and certification shall be published in the
Federal Register
and shall be transmitted, along with the accompanying Memorandum of Justification, to Congress.
Dated: September 30, 2026.
Marco Rubio,
Secretary of State, U.S. Department of State.
